Evolution iteration 1 is complete.

## What happened

**Stage 1 — Lineage analysis.** The graph had only the evaluated baseline (`ea3b299` / tree `9f49dd72…`, average **0.4367**: USPTO 0.20, Symptom2Disease 0.80, LawBench 0.31). Reading the traces, the sharpest evidence was that LawBench's loss was concentrated in answer *wording*: 20 of 69 wrong answers differed from the target only by a trailing 「罪」 (43 of 100 predictions carried that suffix while **0 of 200** training answers did), and 13 collapsed a multi-label target. One trace showed the exact wording `单位行贿` sitting in the retrieved context while the answer still came back `单位行贿罪` — the harness never checked its answer against what the memory actually writes.

I also tested two competing hypotheses offline before committing to one: relevance-ranked retrieval would not have helped — all 50 USPTO examples and ~175/200 Symptom examples already fit in the context budget, and ranked selection only doubled LawBench answer coverage. So the memory was not the bottleneck; answer fidelity was.

**Stage 2 — Evolution.** `prepare_memory.py` now derives an answer profile from the training answers (literal items, separators, repetition/length statistics); a vocabulary-like memory is detected from those statistics alone (Symptom 22 items/200, LawBench 175/327, USPTO 50 distinct in 50 → out of scope). A new `AnswerVerificationMiddleware` gives the model exactly one repair turn when its final answer contains an item that is a near-variant of one the memory writes, quoting the memory's own wording. Verified offline with a scripted stub model and on baseline traces (28 wrong flagged, 0 correct flagged) before the single evaluation run.

**Result:** `{"USPTO": 0.25, "Symptom2Disease": 0.82, "LawBench": 0.41, "average": 0.4933, "status": "partial"}` — **0.4367 → 0.4933**. The repair fired in exactly the 28 predicted LawBench samples (nowhere else); 「罪」-suffixed predictions fell 43 → 20; the remaining 20 are precisely the cases whose target wording is absent from the memory, where the check stays silent by design. I recorded honestly in the note that only ~6 of the 14 LawBench wrong→correct flips are attributable to the mechanism (the rest, plus all of USPTO/Symptom's movement, is run-to-run variance), and flagged the one regression plus the multi-label-collapse bucket as iteration-2 material.

The evaluated commit `d7b155f` on `codex/answer-convention-repair` matches the run's tree hash exactly, with its evolution note attached.
